claims.quote: the much more practicable thing is that upper footpath, with these moving platforms beside it, running out over the street after the manner of the viaduct of an elevated railroad.
claims.description: City streets gain elevated footpaths with moving platforms alongside.

claims.quote: Will this diversion of the vast omnibus traffic of to-day into the air and underground, together with the segregation of van traffic to specific routes and times, be the only change in the streets of the new century?
claims.description: Omnibus traffic moves onto elevated and underground routes while delivery vans are restricted to set routes and times.

claims.quote: I must confess I do not see what is to prevent the process of elimination that is beginning now with the heavy vans spreading until it covers all horse traffic
claims.description: Horse traffic disappears from city streets, leaving cleaner, better-drained roads for soft-tired vehicles and cyclists.

claims.quote: there is no reason but the existing filth why the roadways should not have translucent *velaria* to pull over in bright sunshine and wet weather.
claims.description: Streets are covered by retractable translucent awnings for sun and rain.

claims.quote: Their advent will be the beginning of the end for steam traction on land and of the steam ship at sea: the end indeed of the Age of Coal and Steam.
claims.description: Portable energy-storage or explosive engines will displace steam power on land and sea.

claims.quote: There can be little doubt that the sea speeds of 50 and even 60 miles an hour will be attained within the next few years.
claims.description: Turbine ships will reach 50 to 60 miles per hour at sea.

claims.quote: a rail along the sea bottom, which would serve as a guide to swift submarine vessels, out of reach of all that superficial "motion" that is so distressing, and of all possibilities of collision
claims.description: Swift submarine ferries are guided by a rail on the sea floor, avoiding waves and collisions.

claims.quote: There is hardly any reason, beyond this tradition of the horse, why the railway carriage should not be even nine or ten feet wide
claims.description: Railway carriages could be made nine or ten feet wide with springs that remove vibration and the comforts of a room.

claims.quote: I do not think it at all probable that aeronautics will ever come into play as a serious modification of transport and communication
claims.description: Flying will not become a serious means of transport or communication.

claims.quote: sea velocities of fifty miles an hour, and land travel at the rate of a hundred, and even cab and omnibus journeys of thirty or forty miles, were shown to be possible
claims.description: Land travel at 100 mph, sea travel at 50 mph and urban road journeys of 30 to 40 miles an hour become feasible.

claims.quote: It is much more probable that these coming cities will not be, in the old sense, cities at all; they will present a new and entirely different phase of human distribution.
claims.description: Great cities will disperse and diffuse over wide regions rather than grow ever denser.

claims.quote: the London citizen of the year 2000 a.d. may have a choice of nearly all England and Wales south of Nottingham and east of Exeter as his suburb
claims.description: Faster transport lets city workers live in suburbs spread over most of southern England by 2000.

claims.quote: the available area for the social equivalent of the favoured season-ticket holders of to-day will have a radius of over one hundred miles, and be almost equal to the area of Ireland.
claims.description: Commuting range for well-off city workers will extend to a radius of over one hundred miles.

claims.quote: they will go well over twenty millions; and that New York, Philadelphia, and Chicago will probably, and Hankow almost certainly, reach forty millions.
claims.description: Metropolitan regions such as London, Berlin and New York will exceed twenty to forty million inhabitants.

claims.quote: this "Democracy," or Wholesale method of living, like the railways, is transient—a first makeshift development of a great and finally (to me at least) quite hopeful social reorganization.
claims.description: Mass uniform ways of living will give way to a more individual and hopeful social reorganization.
